body:
Fixes #5994.

## What

`output_buffer::grow()` in `detail/view/serializer.hpp` compared the output size with `m_out.capacity()` to decide how far a growth step may go and whether to `reserve()`. `capacity()` is not part of the StringType requirements, so `basic_json_view::dump()` did not compile with the tests' `alt_string`.

The buffer now remembers what it last passed to `reserve()` (`m_reserved`, initialized to the estimate). That is a lower bound of the real capacity, so the growth steps behave as before; at worst a `reserve()` is issued that the string would not have needed, which is then a no-op.

## Docs

`template_parameters.md`, StringType "Required for other functionality": `basic_json_view::dump` needs `reserve(n)` and `resize(n)` (one argument); `capacity()` is not required.

## Tests

`unit-alt-string.cpp`, new test case "alternative string type with json_view": a read-only document over `alt_json` (dump plain, indented, ensure_ascii, against `alt_json::dump()`; materialize; `contains`/`operator[]` with `alt_string` keys), a dump large enough for several growth steps, and an editable document (`set`, `push_back`, `save()`/`load()`). Without the fix, the file does not compile (`no member named 'capacity' in 'alt_string'`); with it, it passes under C++11 and C++17 (Apple clang).

## Public API

No breaking changes.

comments.body:
### Performance check

**No performance impact.** `output_buffer::grow()` now tracks the reserved size in a member instead of calling `capacity()`. `grow()` only runs when the size estimate is exceeded, so this is a cold path.

- **Generated code** (clang, arm64): two functions differ. `output_buffer::grow()` is **one 16-byte block shorter**, because it no longer decodes libc++'s short-string capacity. The `dump()` entry stores the new member, which is one or two instructions per `dump()` call. Everything else is identical.
- **Instruction counts**: all 38 rows are within ±0.4 %. The view `dump()` rows (twitter 1.0001, citm_catalog 1.0005, canada 1.0006, ensure_ascii twitter 1.0008) sit inside the noise band. The rows with identical code move by the same +0.05–0.1 %.
- With the default `std::string`, growth is the same up to allocator rounding. `m_reserved` is the last size passed to `reserve()`, so it never exceeds `capacity()`. Doubling now starts from the requested size instead of the rounded capacity. If the caller passes a string that already has more capacity, the extra `reserve()` is a no-op, so the number of reallocations does not grow.

<details><summary>Method</summary>

- PR head vs. its base (merge base), both compiled into one binary (namespaces renamed per copy) with the same workload: DOM parse (string, stream, callback), copy/destroy, `==`/`<`, iteration, `dump()`, msgpack/UBJSON/BJData read and write, `json_document` parse/`dump()`/`==`/`get<std::int64_t>()` on twitter, citm_catalog, canada and small_signed_ints.
- **Generated code**: both variants disassembled (Apple clang 21, `-O3`, arm64), names and addresses masked, compared function by function.
- **Instruction counts**: Apple M1 Max, instructions retired per repetition (minimum of 3 runs, setup subtracted). Rows whose machine code is identical vary by about ±0.4 %, which is the noise floor. Where a hot path changes, also GCC 13.3 `-O3` on x86-64 under callgrind, which gives exact counts (built with `-falign-functions=64 -falign-loops=64` unless a row says otherwise).
</details>

---

https://www.cppreference.com/cpp/string/basic_string/reserve

> (until C++20)
> If new_cap is less than the current [capacity()](https://www.cppreference.com/cpp/string/basic_string/capacity), this is a non-binding shrink request.
> If new_cap is less than the current [size()](https://www.cppreference.com/cpp/string/basic_string/size), this is a non-binding shrink-to-fit request equivalent to [shrink_to_fit()](https://www.cppreference.com/cpp/string/basic_string/shrink_to_fit)(since C++11).

I don't know if any library actually implemented that shrink request.  I assume not, since it was changed to a no-op for C++20.
I think it's probably safe, I just wanted you to confirm for yourself that you also think it's safe.

linked_issues.body:
### Description

`basic_json_view::dump()` (json_view, merged 2026-10-21) does not compile with a `StringType` that satisfies the documented StringType requirements but has no `capacity()` member. The library's own reference for the minimal `StringType` is the `alt_string` class in `tests/src/unit-alt-string.cpp`: `basic_json<std::map, std::vector, alt_string>` compiles and passes its unit test, but `basic_json_document<...>::parse(...)` followed by `root().dump()` fails with

```
include/nlohmann/detail/view/serializer.hpp:120:83: error: no member named 'capacity' in 'alt_string'
```

`capacity()` is the only missing piece: with a one-line `capacity()` added to `alt_string`, parse, dump (plain, indented, ensure_ascii), materialize, `get<alt_json>`, `find`/`at`/`operator[]`/`contains`/`count` with `alt_string` keys, `items()`, `shrink_to_fit()`, `memory_usage()`, and the editable document's `set`/`push_back`/`save()`/`load()` all compile and run correctly.

The DOM never calls `capacity()` on `string_t`; the StringType section of `docs/mkdocs/docs/features/types/template_parameters.md` does not list it (it lists `reserve(n)` only for "JSON Pointer, flatten, diff", so the view's `reserve()` call is a second requirement the docs do not tie to dump; `alt_string` happens to have it). Nothing under `docs/mkdocs/docs/api/basic_json_view`, `basic_json_document` or `features/json_view.md` mentions StringType requirements, and no json_view test instantiates `alt_string`, which is why CI did not catch it.

### Reproduction steps

```sh
clang++ -std=c++17 -I include -I tests/src view_alt.cpp   # alt_string copied from tests/src/unit-alt-string.cpp
```

### Expected vs. actual results

Expected: json_view compiles with every `StringType` that `basic_json` accepts (or the extra requirement is documented in `template_parameters.md` and checked by a test).

Actual: compile error in `detail/view/serializer.hpp:120`.

### Minimal code example

```cpp
#include <map>
#include <vector>
#include <nlohmann/json.hpp>
#include <nlohmann/json_view.hpp>
#include "alt_string.hpp"   // the class from tests/src/unit-alt-string.cpp
using alt_json = nlohmann::basic_json<std::map, std::vector, alt_string>;
int main()
{
    auto d = nlohmann::basic_json_document<alt_json, nlohmann::view_mode::read_only>::parse("{\"a\":[1,\"x\"]}");
    alt_json m = d.root().materialize();   // fine
    (void)d.root().dump();                 // error: no member named 'capacity' in 'alt_string'
}
```

### Error messages

```
include/nlohmann/detail/view/serializer.hpp:120:83: error: no member named 'capacity' in 'alt_string'
    const std::size_t size = (std::max)((std::min)(m_out.size() + step, m_out.capacity()), used + n + 256);
```
instantiated from `output_buffer<alt_string>::grow` ← `reserve` ← `dump_text` ← `dump_ascii` ← `basic_json_view::dump` (`json_view.hpp:665`).

### Compiler and operating system

Apple clang 17 (libc++) and gcc 16 (libstdc++); the error is compiler-independent.

### Library version

develop at ddc34f546a (json_view only; 3.12.0 has no json_view).

### Validation

- [x] The bug also occurs if the latest version from the [`develop`](https://github.com/nlohmann/json/tree/develop) branch is used.
- [x] I can successfully [compile and run the unit tests](https://github.com/nlohmann/json#execute-unit-tests).

### Root cause

[`include/nlohmann/detail/view/serializer.hpp:119-123`](https://github.com/nlohmann/json/blob/ddc34f546a/include/nlohmann/detail/view/serializer.hpp#L119-L123): `output_buffer::grow()` compares `m_out.size() + step` with `m_out.capacity()` to decide how much to `reserve()`.

### Suggested fix

Track the reserved size in `output_buffer` itself (`m_reserved`, set after each `reserve()`; the string may reserve more, so this is a lower bound that costs at most one extra `reserve()`), and use it instead of `m_out.capacity()`. Then add an `alt_string` instantiation of json_view (parse, dump, materialize, editable set/push_back, save/load) to the tests, so the view keeps to the same StringType contract as the DOM. If `capacity()` is meant to be required instead, add it to the StringType requirements in `template_parameters.md` and to the tests' `alt_string`.

---
*Found during a bug hunt on develop; written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.*
